_note: Evals use bundled synthetic fixtures (see files/make_fixtures.py, files/make_extra_fixtures.py, files/make_tier1_fixtures.py) rather than nilearn.datasets fetchers, because Anthropic's sandbox blocks the CDN hosts the fetchers download from. End users with normal internet should use the built-in fetchers — the skill recommends them by default.

evals.name: glm_first_level_block_design
evals.prompt: I have a small task-fMRI dataset and I want to fit a first-level GLM. The BOLD file is at evals/files/glm/bold.nii.gz with TR=7s, the events are in evals/files/glm/events.tsv (a single trial type called 'active' in a block design), and there's a brain mask at evals/files/glm/brain_mask.nii.gz. Please fit the model, compute the contrast for 'active' vs baseline, save the z-map and a glass-brain visualization to ./results_glm/, and tell me what z-range you saw. Also generate an HTML report and save the design matrix as a PNG.
evals.expected_output: A working FirstLevelModel fit on the provided fixture, with t_r=7 set explicitly, the 'active' contrast computed and saved as a NIfTI, glass-brain PNG saved, HTML report generated via model.generate_report() (not deprecated make_glm_report), design matrix plot saved, smoothing_fwhm documented, and a written summary that includes the actual z-range observed.
expectations: Reads bold.nii.gz from evals/files/glm/ (does not invent a different path or call a nilearn dataset fetcher)
Loads events.tsv as a DataFrame with onset, duration, trial_type columns
Instantiates FirstLevelModel with t_r=7.0 (or 7) explicitly
Calls .fit() on the model with the bold image and events
Calls .compute_contrast('active', ...) (or equivalent) and gets a z-map
Saves at least one .nii.gz file to ./results_glm/
Saves at least one .png file (e.g., glass brain or stat map) to ./results_glm/
Generates HTML report using model.generate_report() — not the deprecated standalone make_glm_report function
Saves design matrix visualization using plot_design_matrix to ./results_glm/
Documents smoothing_fwhm: explicitly sets it (e.g., smoothing_fwhm=5.0) or explicitly states no smoothing was applied
Reports the actual z-range in the response text (not a placeholder)
Uses standardize=False (or omits it; the default is False for FirstLevelModel) and not the deprecated 'True' value for any maskers used

evals.name: connectivity_three_subjects_correlation
evals.prompt: I have 3 subjects of resting-state fMRI in evals/files/connectivity/ — files are sub-01_bold.nii.gz, sub-02_bold.nii.gz, sub-03_bold.nii.gz with TR=2s and matching sub-XX_confounds.tsv files. There's a 6-region label atlas at evals/files/connectivity/atlas.nii.gz with names in atlas_labels.csv. Extract timeseries for each subject (use the confounds), compute correlation matrices, and give me a mean matrix heatmap plus a glass-brain connectome. Output to ./connectivity_out/.
evals.expected_output: Three-subject correlation pipeline: NiftiLabelsMasker built from atlas.nii.gz with t_r=2 and bandpass filter set, timeseries extracted for each subject with their matching confounds, a correlation matrix per subject, a mean matrix, a heatmap PNG, and a connectome glass-brain PNG.
expectations: Uses NiftiLabelsMasker (not NiftiMapsMasker — atlas is deterministic labels)
Constructs masker with t_r=2.0 explicitly
Constructs masker with standardize='zscore_sample' (the string, not deprecated True)
Sets low_pass and high_pass on the masker (or filters before extraction)
Loads each subject's matching confounds TSV and passes to fit_transform
Uses ConnectivityMeasure with kind='correlation'
Produces 3 timeseries arrays of shape (150, 6) (or fit_transform on a list)
Computes a per-subject and a mean connectivity matrix
Saves a matrix heatmap PNG to ./connectivity_out/
Saves a glass-brain connectome PNG using plot_connectome with coords
Mean matrix shows strong positive correlation between regions 1-2 and 3-4, negative between 5-6 (the known structure in the fixture)

evals.name: decoding_face_vs_house_leave_one_run_out
evals.prompt: Run an MVPA decoding analysis: the 4D BOLD is at evals/files/decoding/bold.nii.gz where each volume is one trial (TR=2s). Labels and run numbers are in evals/files/decoding/labels.csv (columns 'labels' with 'face'/'house', 'chunks' with run number 0-5). Use the VT mask at evals/files/decoding/vt_mask.nii.gz, SVC classifier, and leave-one-run-out cross-validation. Tell me the mean accuracy across folds and how it compares to chance. Save the weight map as a NIfTI and a plot to ./decoder_out/.
evals.expected_output: Decoder pipeline with SVC, LeaveOneGroupOut CV on the run variable, fit on the VT mask, accuracy reported with chance level (0.5), weight map saved as NIfTI and PNG.
expectations: Loads labels.csv and uses the 'labels' column as y and 'chunks' as groups
Uses nilearn.decoding.Decoder (not raw sklearn) with estimator='svc'
Uses LeaveOneGroupOut from sklearn.model_selection (or equivalent group CV)
Passes groups=chunks to decoder.fit()
Uses the vt_mask.nii.gz as the mask= argument (not whole brain)
Uses standardize='zscore_sample' (not deprecated True)
Reports mean accuracy in the response text
Reports the chance level (0.5 for binary) in the response text
Saves the weight map as a .nii.gz in ./decoder_out/
Saves a plot of the weight map as PNG in ./decoder_out/

evals.name: glm_statistical_thresholding_fdr
evals.prompt: I've already decided to use the GLM fixture from evals/files/glm/: bold.nii.gz (TR=7s), events.tsv (trial type 'active'), and brain_mask.nii.gz. Fit a first-level GLM, compute the 'active' contrast z-map, then apply FDR thresholding at alpha=0.05 using nilearn.glm.threshold_stats_img. Report the FDR threshold value, how many voxels survive, and the peak z-score in the surviving map. Save both the unthresholded and thresholded z-maps as NIfTIs, plus a side-by-side visualization showing unthresholded vs FDR-corrected, to ./results_threshold/.
evals.expected_output: GLM fit → contrast → threshold_stats_img with height_control='fdr', alpha=0.05. Reports the numeric FDR threshold, surviving voxel count, and peak z-score. Saves unthresholded z-map, thresholded z-map, and a comparison PNG.
expectations: Calls nilearn.glm.threshold_stats_img (not just plot_stat_map threshold argument)
Passes height_control='fdr' and alpha=0.05 explicitly
Reports the actual numeric FDR threshold value in the response text
Reports the number of voxels surviving the threshold
Reports the peak z-score in the surviving map
Saves the unthresholded z-map as a .nii.gz in ./results_threshold/
Saves the thresholded z-map as a .nii.gz in ./results_threshold/
Saves at least one PNG visualization to ./results_threshold/
Does not confuse the plot_stat_map threshold argument with statistical inference

evals.name: second_level_group_glm
evals.prompt: I have first-level z-maps from 8 subjects: evals/files/second_level/sub-01_zmap.nii.gz through sub-08_zmap.nii.gz, and a brain mask at evals/files/second_level/brain_mask.nii.gz. Run a second-level (group) GLM to test for a population-level activation (one-sample t-test against zero). Use an intercept-only design matrix. Compute the second-level z-map, apply FDR correction at alpha=0.05, and report where the group activates. Save the group z-map and a glass-brain plot to ./results_group/.
evals.expected_output: SecondLevelModel fit on 8 z-maps with intercept design, contrast computed, FDR thresholding applied, group z-map and glass-brain saved to ./results_group/. Response includes numeric description of where group activation is found.
expectations: Uses nilearn.glm.second_level.SecondLevelModel (not FirstLevelModel)
Builds design matrix with pandas DataFrame containing a single 'intercept' column of ones, length 8
Calls second_level_model.fit(zmaps_list, design_matrix=...)
Calls .compute_contrast() to get the group z-map
Applies threshold_stats_img with height_control='fdr', alpha=0.05
Saves group z-map as .nii.gz in ./results_group/
Saves a glass-brain PNG in ./results_group/
Reports the location or extent of group-level activation in the response

evals.name: seed_based_connectivity
evals.prompt: I have one subject's resting-state BOLD at evals/files/connectivity/sub-01_bold.nii.gz (TR=2s) and confounds at evals/files/connectivity/sub-01_confounds.tsv. Run a seed-based connectivity analysis: use a 6mm-radius sphere centered at MNI (-16, -16, 0) as the seed ROI (this is region_1 in the atlas). Extract the seed timeseries with NiftiSpheresMasker, extract whole-brain voxel timeseries with NiftiMasker (using the atlas as mask — or the brain implicitly), regress out confounds for both, then compute the correlation between the seed timeseries and every brain voxel. Save the seed correlation map as a NIfTI and a glass-brain plot to ./seed_out/. Report the peak correlation value.
evals.expected_output: NiftiSpheresMasker seed extraction + NiftiMasker whole-brain extraction, correlation computed, seed-map saved as NIfTI and plotted. Peak correlation reported.
expectations: Uses NiftiSpheresMasker with seeds=[(-16, -16, 0)] and radius=6 (or nearby value)
Passes t_r=2.0 to NiftiSpheresMasker
Uses standardize='zscore_sample' (not deprecated True) for both maskers
Passes confounds to fit_transform for both maskers
Computes voxel-wise correlation between seed timeseries and brain timeseries (e.g. np.corrcoef or stats.pearsonr)
Builds a NIfTI image from the correlation array using the masker's inverse_transform or nibabel directly
Saves seed correlation map as .nii.gz in ./seed_out/
Saves a glass-brain PNG in ./seed_out/
Reports the peak (maximum) correlation value in the response

evals.name: niftimasker_signal_extraction_tsnr
evals.prompt: Use evals/files/glm/bold.nii.gz (TR=7s) and evals/files/glm/brain_mask.nii.gz to compute a temporal SNR (tSNR) map. tSNR = mean(timeseries) / std(timeseries) per voxel — so you must NOT detrend or standardize before computing it (detrending removes the mean, which is the signal denominator for tSNR). Use NiftiMasker with standardize=False and detrend=False to extract the raw signal. After computing tSNR, report the median tSNR across brain voxels and save the tSNR map as a NIfTI and a stat-map PNG to ./tsnr_out/.
evals.expected_output: NiftiMasker extraction with standardize=False, detrend=False (raw signal preserved so tSNR mean is nonzero). tSNR = mean/std per voxel. Median tSNR > 1 reported. tSNR NIfTI and PNG saved.
expectations: Uses NiftiMasker with mask_img pointing to brain_mask.nii.gz
Sets standardize=False on the masker (raw signal units, not z-scores)
Sets detrend=False on the masker (mean must be preserved for tSNR numerator)
Extracted timeseries has shape (96, n_voxels) — 96 timepoints
Computes tSNR = mean(axis=0) / std(axis=0) per voxel
Median tSNR across voxels is greater than 1 (synthetic data baseline ~100, noise ~5)
Reports the median tSNR value in the response text
Converts tSNR array back to a NIfTI image using masker.inverse_transform
Saves tSNR NIfTI to ./tsnr_out/
Saves a stat-map or brain-map PNG to ./tsnr_out/

evals.name: multirun_first_level_glm
evals.prompt: I have two runs of task fMRI: evals/files/multirun/run-01_bold.nii.gz and run-02_bold.nii.gz (TR=7s, 48 volumes each), with matching events in run-01_events.tsv and run-02_events.tsv (trial type 'active', same block design in each run), and a brain mask at evals/files/multirun/brain_mask.nii.gz. Fit a single FirstLevelModel across both runs (pass both BOLD files and both event DataFrames as lists), compute the 'active' contrast, and compare the z-map peak to what you'd get from run-01 alone. Save z-maps and glass-brain plots for the combined model and run-01-only model to ./multirun_out/. Report both peak z-scores.
evals.expected_output: FirstLevelModel fit with a list of two BOLD images and a list of two events DataFrames, contrast computed from combined model, comparison with single-run model. Both peak z-scores reported, z-maps and plots saved.
expectations: Passes a list of two NIfTI images to FirstLevelModel.fit(), not a single concatenated image
Passes a list of two events DataFrames (one per run) to .fit()
Sets t_r=7.0 explicitly
Fits a second model on run-01 alone for comparison
Calls .compute_contrast('active') on both models
Reports peak z-score for the combined model in the response text
Reports peak z-score for the single-run model in the response text
Combined model peak z-score should be >= single-run peak (more data = more power)
Saves z-maps as .nii.gz in ./multirun_out/
Saves glass-brain PNGs to ./multirun_out/

evals.name: atlas_space_mismatch_resampling
evals.prompt: I have resting-state BOLD at evals/files/space_mismatch/bold.nii.gz (4mm voxels, TR=2s, 150 volumes) and a 6-region label atlas at evals/files/space_mismatch/atlas_2mm.nii.gz — note that the atlas is at 2mm resolution while the BOLD is 4mm (different affine and shape). Confounds are in evals/files/space_mismatch/confounds.tsv. Extract per-region timeseries using NiftiLabelsMasker and compute a 6×6 correlation matrix. Handle the space mismatch so you don't get a shape error or a wrong number of regions. Save a heatmap of the correlation matrix to ./space_out/.
evals.expected_output: Atlas resampled to BOLD space before masker, NiftiLabelsMasker extracts timeseries of shape (150, 6), correlation matrix shape (6, 6) with known structure, heatmap saved to ./space_out/.
expectations: Detects or explicitly handles the space mismatch (atlas 2mm vs BOLD 4mm — different affine/shape)
Uses nilearn.image.resample_to_img(atlas, bold_img, interpolation='nearest') to resample the label atlas to BOLD space (or equivalent resampling before masking)
Uses NiftiLabelsMasker (not NiftiMapsMasker — atlas is discrete labels)
Constructs masker with t_r=2.0 explicitly
Uses standardize='zscore_sample' (not deprecated True)
Passes confounds to fit_transform
Produces timeseries of shape (150, 6) — 6 regions, not 1 or some other number
Uses ConnectivityMeasure with kind='correlation' to compute the 6×6 matrix
Saves a heatmap PNG to ./space_out/

evals.name: glm_multicontrast_face_house
evals.prompt: I have a two-condition event-related fMRI task: BOLD at evals/files/glm_multicontrast/bold.nii.gz (TR=2s, 120 volumes), events at evals/files/glm_multicontrast/events.tsv (trial_type column contains 'face' and 'house'), brain mask at evals/files/glm_multicontrast/brain_mask.nii.gz. Fit a first-level GLM and compute three contrasts: (1) face > house, (2) house > face, and (3) an F-contrast testing whether face OR house differs from baseline (i.e., the omnibus test for any task effect). Save all three stat maps and glass-brain plots to ./multicontrast_out/. Report the peak stat value for each.
evals.expected_output: FirstLevelModel fit with face+house events, three contrasts computed: face>house (t), house>face (t), F-contrast for both conditions. All stat maps saved. Peak stats reported.
expectations: Instantiates FirstLevelModel with t_r=2.0
Fits model with events.tsv containing both 'face' and 'house' trial_types
Computes face > house contrast using string formula ('face - house') or contrast vector
Computes house > face contrast
Computes an F-contrast testing both face and house vs baseline — not just a second t-test
F-contrast uses a 2D numpy contrast matrix (two rows) or 'effects of interest' string with stat_type='F' — not compute_contrast('face + house') which is a t-test
Passes stat_type='F' explicitly to compute_contrast for the F-contrast (not 't')
Correctly distinguishes between t-contrasts (directional, signed) and the F-contrast (omnibus, unsigned) in the response text
Saves at least 3 stat map .nii.gz files to ./multicontrast_out/
Saves glass-brain PNGs for at least 2 contrasts to ./multicontrast_out/
Reports peak stat for face > house in response text

evals.name: decoder_regressor_continuous_labels
evals.prompt: I have 90 trial volumes at evals/files/regression/bold.nii.gz (TR=2s, each volume = one trial). Each trial has a continuous orientation angle (0–180°) in evals/files/regression/labels.csv (columns: 'angle' and 'chunks' for run number, 5 runs of 18 trials). Use the V1 ROI mask at evals/files/regression/v1_mask.nii.gz. Fit a regression decoder to predict the continuous stimulus orientation using leave-one-run-out CV. Report the cross-validated R² score and compare it to chance (R²=0). Save the weight map as a NIfTI and a glass-brain plot to ./regression_out/.
evals.expected_output: DecoderRegressor (not Decoder) with SVR or ridge estimator, LeaveOneGroupOut CV, R² metric, weight map saved as NIfTI and plotted.
expectations: Uses nilearn.decoding.DecoderRegressor (not nilearn.decoding.Decoder for classification)
Uses a regression estimator: estimator='svr' or 'ridge' (not 'svc' or 'logistic')
Uses v1_mask.nii.gz as the mask= argument
Uses LeaveOneGroupOut or equivalent group-based CV (not KFold ignoring run structure)
Passes groups=chunks (run numbers) to decoder.fit()
Uses standardize='zscore_sample' (not deprecated True)
Reports the cross-validated R² score (or r_pairwise) in the response text
Notes that chance R² is 0 (baseline for regression, not 0.5 as in classification)
Saves weight map as .nii.gz to ./regression_out/
Saves a glass-brain or stat-map plot as PNG to ./regression_out/

evals.name: connectivity_tangent_space
evals.prompt: I have the same 3-subject resting-state data as before: evals/files/connectivity/sub-0{1,2,3}_bold.nii.gz (TR=2s) with confounds and the 6-region atlas. This time compute connectivity using the tangent space method (kind='tangent') instead of Pearson correlation. Explain what the tangent method does differently from correlation and what values you would expect on the diagonal of a tangent matrix. Compute the tangent matrices, report the mean off-diagonal value, and save a heatmap to ./tangent_out/.
evals.expected_output: ConnectivityMeasure(kind='tangent') producing (3, 6, 6) matrices; diagonal elements near zero (not 1.0); explanation of tangent space projection; mean off-diagonal reported; heatmap saved.
expectations: Uses NiftiLabelsMasker with t_r=2.0 and standardize='zscore_sample'
Uses ConnectivityMeasure with kind='tangent' (not kind='correlation')
Correctly explains that tangent projects covariance matrices to the tangent space at the geometric mean across subjects
Correctly notes that diagonal elements of tangent matrices are approximately zero (unlike correlation where diagonal=1)
Produces connectivity matrices of shape (3, 6, 6) — one per subject
Reports the mean off-diagonal value in the response
Saves a connectivity heatmap PNG to ./tangent_out/
Does not confuse tangent output with correlation (diagonal should not be forced to 1 or described as 1)
Notes that tangent is recommended for downstream ML on connectivity (not raw correlation)

evals.name: cluster_level_thresholding
evals.prompt: Fit a GLM on evals/files/glm/ (bold.nii.gz TR=7s, events.tsv with 'active' condition, brain_mask.nii.gz). Use nilearn.reporting.get_clusters_table to produce a table of significant clusters with their peak MNI coordinates, peak z-score, and cluster size (as would go in a paper's Table 1). Print the table, report how many clusters were found, and save the thresholded z-map and a visualization to ./cluster_out/.
evals.expected_output: GLM fit → z-map → get_clusters_table(z_map, stat_threshold=2.5, cluster_threshold=10). Cluster table printed with peak coordinates, peak stat, cluster size. Number of clusters reported. Thresholded map and visualization saved.

Calls nilearn.reporting.get_clusters_table (not threshold_stats_img for the table)
Passes stat_threshold (e.g., 2.5) to get_clusters_table
Passes cluster_threshold (minimum cluster size in voxels, e.g., 10) to get_clusters_table
Produces a pandas DataFrame (not just an image) with cluster information
Cluster table includes columns for peak MNI coordinates (X, Y, Z) and cluster size
Prints or displays the cluster table in the response
Reports the number of clusters found in the response text
Saves thresholded z-map or stat map .nii.gz to ./cluster_out/
Saves a PNG visualization to ./cluster_out/

evals.prompt: Using the GLM fixture evals/files/glm/ (bold.nii.gz TR=7s, events.tsv, brain_mask.nii.gz), fit a first-level GLM, compute the 'active' contrast z-map, and create interactive HTML visualizations — not just static PNGs.
